lab.title: Create the first genuine asynchronous persistence boundary
lab.objective: Add EF Core SQLite to Infrastructure.
lab.task: Persist and retrieve an open ClockEntry through SQLite without replacing the earlier synchronous in-memory repository.
lab.startingCondition: Production remains synchronous and in-memory through Session 30B. Session 31 deliberately adds SQLite I/O, a separate async repository contract, and EF Core async calls for the first time.

steps.text: Step 1/12: Delete only the unused Infrastructure/Class1.cs template placeholder.

Step 2/12: In Infrastructure.csproj, reference Domain and add Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite version 10.0.10, Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions version 10.0.10, and the patched SQLitePCLRaw.bundle_e_sqlite3 version 2.1.12.
Step 3/12: In Domain/Repositories, create IAsyncClockEntryRepository.cs with SaveClockEntryAsync and GetOpenClockEntryAsync. Each method accepts CancellationToken cancellationToken = default.
Step 4/12: Build the Domain and Infrastructure projects before implementing the repository.
Step 5/12: In Infrastructure, create sealed ClockEntryEntity with Id, EmployeeId, ClockIn, and nullable Clockout properties.
Step 6/12: In Infrastructure, create sealed TimeClockDbContext : DbContext, accept DbContextOptions<TimeClockDbContext>, and expose DbSet<ClockEntryEntity> ClockEntries.
Step 7/12: In Infrastructure, create sealed EfClockEntryRepository : IAsyncClockEntryRepository and inject TimeClockDbContext through its constructor.

Step 8/12: Inside SaveClockEntryAsync, map the domain ClockEntry to ClockEntryEntity, call Add, then await SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken). Task promises completion; await observes the database operation and does not itself mean another thread.
Step 9/12: Inside GetOpenClockEntryAsync, query the matching open row with FirstOrDefaultAsync and forward cancellationToken. Map a found entity back to ClockEntry.
Step 10/12: In Domain/Services, create sealed AsyncClockEntryService, inject IAsyncClockEntryRepository, and add TryClockInAsync that checks for an open entry before saving.
Step 11/12: In the test project, reference Infrastructure and add EfClockEntryRepositoryTests.cs using an open in-memory SQLite connection.
Step 12/12: Run EfClockEntryRepositoryTests, then build the full Release solution and run every test with --no-build.

reveals.title: Solution
reveals.text: The completed repository maps ClockEntry to ClockEntryEntity and awaits the genuine EF Core I/O calls.
